pairs.subject: node-boot-and-declarative-bootstrap
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/main.rs:397 The first-start price seed is detected by an empty book. On SQLite and Postgres it is written in one transaction, so the transaction serves as the marker. On the Firestore backend, which this same boot selects at main.rs:388, seed_prices falls back to the Store trait's row-by-row default (crates/store/src/lib.rs:1410). A crash partway through therefore leaves a non-empty partial book that no later start will finish, which is the exact failure the technique names.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/main.rs:397 Emptiness detection with no marker. Atomicity depends on the backend: SQLite prices::seed (unchecked_transaction) and Postgres prices::seed (pool.begin) commit as one unit. store-firestore does not override seed_prices, so it inherits the row-by-row default, and the trait doc itself admits this 'keeps that half-seed hazard'.

crates/api/src/main.rs:484 Boot order: logging, then the credential-boundary refusal (line 351, before the store opens), then store open and seed, then state, then bind. The 'listening' line logs the bound local_addr (485/507), and background sweeps spawn only after the bind. There is no unseal-shaped step, so the replay-diagnostic part of the technique is outside its 'earns its cost' scope. Minor: list_projects().unwrap_or_default() at line 415 silently warms an empty policy cache if the store errors.

crates/api/src/main.rs:340 All configuration is env read once at boot. Grepping crates/api/src for sighup/reload found no reload handler, so every key is effectively restart-only, which is the technique's 'when not to use' case.

crates/api/src/main.rs:394 Config seeds prices once, and from then on the API (PUT /v1/prices) owns them. That is the technique's 'seeded ordinary API object' exclusion. No device kind here is born from both config and the API.

crates/api/src/main.rs:398 The only first-start act is a data-row seed. There is no declarative bootstrap file of privileged requests (no policy or auth creation), so there is nothing to shape as a request chain.
crates/api/src/main.rs:391 Storage is opened directly and has no sealing boundary. Grepping crates/api/src for seal/unseal found nothing, so there is no pre-unseal component catalog.
